paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
model_annotation: The figure is a two-level donut (nested pie) chart showing the distribution of samples across two ambiguity-related measures, with the outer ring representing “Ambiguity Std” categories and the inner ring representing “Max Ambiguity” categories; in total, there are 4 slices in the outer ring and 3 slices in the inner ring. In the outer ring, the slices are labeled (via the legend) as Std: 0.0 (dark teal-blue) at about 49.0%, Std: 0.47 (medium blue) at about 39.0%, Std: 0.82 (brighter blue) at about 5.0%, and Std: 0.94 (light cyan-blue) at about 7.0%, with percentage labels displayed directly on the ring. In the inner ring, the slices correspond (via the legend) to Max: 1 (medium-light blue) at about 39.0%, Max: 2 (slightly darker light blue) at about 47.7%, and Max: 3 (very pale blue) at about 14.2%, also labeled with percentages inside the slices. Two separate legends appear on the right—one for the outer ring (“Ambiguity Std (Outer)”) and one for the inner ring (“Max Ambiguity (Inner)”)—and no slices appear exploded or otherwise visually emphasized; the segments are arranged around the circle without an explicitly indicated ordering scheme beyond their placement.
